RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-female panel alone is not evidence of discrimination or bias. In academic hiring—especially for lecturer positions rather than research-track professorships—departments frequently prioritize relevant industry background, specific curriculum needs, and interview performance over sheer publication count or degree completion status. 

Additionally, two weeks is a standard administrative window; delayed written feedback is typical at public universities and does not indicate foul play. Raising the panel's gender composition without concrete evidence of procedural misconduct will appear unprofessional, damage your academic reputation, and harm future job prospects. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback on how to strengthen your profile for future roles.
